steps.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: revised photorealistic bridge concept, landscape 3:2.
Input image 1 is the edit target. Remake the SAME woodland suspension footbridge with the following specific corrections from an independent design critic. Keep its slender timber footbridge identity, weathered blue-gray steel, clear stony river, mixed forest, natural late-morning light and photographic realism. Preserve the general near-left / far-right composition, but pull the camera back and raise it slightly enough to see the approaches, portal openings and anchorages. A single coherent image, no collage, text, labels, people, vehicles or UI.

CRITICAL CORRECTION — WALKABLE PORTALS:
Completely REMOVE the full-height X diagonals inside BOTH transverse tower openings. They currently block the walking route. Replace each tower with two steel legs outside the deck edges, an overhead crossbeam and short upper-corner knee braces well above head clearance. The open rectangle between the legs must remain EMPTY from the deck up for at least three metres. Show continuous timber walking surface passing freely through both portals and onto the banks. No diagonal bar, cable, railing or foundation across this passage. Both towers share this exact construction.

CLEAR CONNECTED STRUCTURE:
Two continuous stranded steel wire-rope main cables, one outside each deck edge, run over recognizable curved steel saddles on the tower crowns and continue as backstays to concrete anchorage blocks set back into BOTH banks. Maintain the same cable material and diameter across the saddles; no segmented rods. Reveal the near cable sockets and embedded anchor hardware, and make the far backstay/anchor path readable beyond its portal rather than lost in leaves. Anchorages and backstays sit outside the walking approaches.
Separate, evenly spaced slender vertical hangers have modest cable clamps at their tops and explicit clevis brackets at their bottoms. Hangers attach to visible restrained dark steel edge girders, never just to the timber fascia. Reveal transverse floor beams and short stringers under the weathered cross-laid timber planks. Keep an elegant shallow deck profile, consistent hanger spacing and two distinct cable planes without impossible intersections.
Continuous metal guardrails with slim vertical infill follow both deck edges, stay clear through the towers, and terminate in proper landing posts. Clear modest gaps between rails, cables and structural members.

GROUNDED LANDINGS:
Show flush deck landings and gently graded gravel walking approaches at both ends. Tower baseplates sit on grouted concrete pedestals with sensible bolts; concrete foundations are embedded within the bank, with irregular stone aprons and coherent damp staining. Do not create isolated columns standing on loose rubble or anchors in the main current. Keep the wide shallow stream naturally flowing around grounded stones, with narrow irregular riffles, subtle transparency and reflections.

COMPOSITION AND FINISH:
Photographic architectural landscape, entire near and far tower crowns in frame, physically coherent perspective, sharp readable bridge geometry and natural surrounding textures. The nearest open portal and uninterrupted deck should be unmistakable. Real rivets and connection plates, subtle restrained paint wear, directional timber grain, natural aggregate concrete. Preserve the original visual quality, warm neutral sunlight and varied woodland, without hiding any structural corrections in fog or vegetation.

Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: complementary approach inspection photograph, landscape 3:2.
Input image 1 is the authoritative revised bridge design. Generate a second view of this EXACT SAME corrected woodland suspension footbridge, retaining the same number and shape of towers, knee braces, steel sections, cables, hanger rhythm, plank deck and bank setting. This is an additional camera of the same design, not a new bridge.

Camera: from the near gravel landing, offset slightly to the river side and modestly above the deck, looking along the walkway THROUGH both portal openings to the opposite gravel landing. The foreground clearly shows the accessible route entering the bridge, a near tower leg and bolted grouted baseplate, the timber-to-steel deck edge and a hanger clevis. Show the shallow steel edge girder and transverse floor beam ends beneath the timber. The far tower and its open passage remain readable. Preserve natural perspective, avoid a telephoto flattening, no fisheye.

CRITICAL INVARIANTS:
Both towers are OPEN PORTALS, each with only an overhead crossbeam and short knee braces at its upper corners. The walking route is completely free of X diagonals, transverse cables and cross rails. Both tower legs stand outside the deck edges. Every visible metre of walkway, including both tower thresholds, is continuous and unobstructed.
There are precisely two continuous stranded wire-rope main cable planes, one outside each side of the walkway. They pass over curved saddles at the tower tops and continue to paired backstay anchors in the banks outside the paths. Do not draw segmented metal bars for the main cable. Individual vertical hangers use smaller saddle clamps and clevises connecting to steel girders rather than wood.
Keep the guardrail design from the hero: straight top rails, evenly spaced posts and neat slender infill, uninterrupted at portal openings. No railing across either landing. The timber deck sits on steel support members with restrained but legible gussets and fasteners.

Keep the same weathered blue-gray painted steel, cross-laid timber planks, realistic lightly stained concrete, grounded bank boulders and gravel approach, lush irregular woodland and clear shallow river. Preserve the hero's natural late-morning daylight and restrained aging. The main purpose is to prove visual continuity of the walking route and believable visible connections. Photorealistic architectural photograph with fine readable material detail, single image, no people, vehicles, labels, text, UI, diagrams or inset panels.
Critic's final check: carry the side guardrails all the way across the exposed short near approach, with properly terminated posts at the gravel landing; keep the centre of the landing fully open.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image 1 is the edit target: the revised bridge approach.
Make ONE tightly targeted correction. The short foreground-RIGHT timber deck edge between the gravel entrance and the near right tower leg is exposed and missing a guardrail. Add a matching short guardrail ONLY along that side edge: a properly bolted end post at the closest right deck corner, a straight rounded handrail, and the same neatly spaced horizontal infill as the existing left approach rail, continuing back to a sensible connection beside the near right tower. The new rail follows the right side of the walking surface, above the riverbank; it does not run across the entrance.
Keep the entire entrance width and the walkway through both portals completely open. Preserve ALL other pixels and design choices as closely as possible: identical camera, landscape, river, light, timber planks, main cables and anchorages, existing railings, steel support members, both open portal towers, the upper-corner knee braces and their geometry. Do not add any X bracing, crossing cable, barrier across the deck, people, text, labels or UI. Same photorealistic quality and 3:2 landscape format.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Input image 1 is the edit target: corrected wide hero image of the woodland footbridge.
Input image 2 is a supporting reference showing the final corrected entrance guardrail of the SAME bridge.
Make one localized correction to image 1, copying the construction shown in image 2: the short exposed timber approach on the near river-facing side needs the matching small guardrail from its entrance corner up to the near tower leg. Add one neatly bolted end post, its rounded top handrail and parallel horizontal infill along that SHORT SIDE EDGE only, matching image 2 and the existing railing. Keep the entrance and entire walking route fully open; no transverse rail across the entrance. The added rail guards only the exposed outside edge between the gravel threshold and tower.
Keep the rest of image 1 unchanged as closely as possible: the wide camera composition, complete open portal towers without X bracing, steel sections, continuous cables, all visible anchorages, timber deck, supports, river, rocks, forest, daylight and realistic material finish. Do not zoom, reframe, replace the landscape, add people or text, or redesign any other bridge component. Single photorealistic landscape image, 3:2.
